interaction_sweep: Shift vs. departure choice: shift is measured from the chosen departure (dispatch-rules.md:21-22,41-42; check_plan.py:94), waiting occurs at customers (dispatch-rules.md:38-40; check_plan.py:83), so a later departure legitimately shortens duration; both sources agree.

Range vs. one route per vehicle: 'range per morning' (dispatch-rules.md:22-23) equals per-route distance because each vehicle runs at most one route (dispatch-rules.md:35); checker applies it per route (check_plan.py:98) - equivalent.
Fleet count vs. route type: count checked after all routes (check_plan.py:101-103) against the per-kind count documented at dispatch-rules.md:18-19,51.
Target file listed inside /app/orders/ is not a morning: instruction.md:1 names the four mornings explicitly, so no ambiguity about a fifth plan.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Checker rejects NaN/Infinity, not stated in rules doc
rejected_candidates.reason: Not a contract gap: these tokens are not JSON and depart/stops must be JSON integers (dispatch-rules.md:58-60); no contract-valid plan is affected.

rejected_candidates.candidate: UTF-8 BOM-prefixed plan would fail json.load (check_plan.py:32-33)
rejected_candidates.reason: Speculative; RFC 8259 JSON text does not carry a BOM and no ordinary JSON writer (e.g. Python json.dump) emits one. Not a reachable grading difference for a competent candidate.

rejected_candidates.reason: Narrative, not graded; cannot affect reward.

reach: No reachable divergence found: every graded rule is defined in candidate-visible dispatch-rules.md and enforced by a checker, orders and targets that are byte-identical to the verifier's copies.
flip: No contract-valid plan identified whose grade would flip under an alternative reasonable reading of instruction.md or dispatch-rules.md.
